data.narrative:
Quaise Energy is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Carlos Araque and Matthew Houde that has raised $134M to date. The relevant peer universe comprises nine companies in the Climate & Energy sector, including eight private firms (Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen among others) and one public comparable (LNZA). However, the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints to support a robust peer-median valuation.

Given this constraint, the Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using total raised ($134M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $268M. This method assumes Quaise will achieve typical milestones warranting a two-fold valuation step between stages.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $228M to $308M, centered on a median of $268M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression estimate. The key uncertainties are (1) the applicability of standard stage-progression multiples to deep-tech climate ventures, which often exhibit nonlinear funding and valuation profiles, and (2) the absence of granular comparable company metrics, which prevents validation via revenue, capital efficiency, or technology-readiness benchmarks. A peer-median approach would require identification of additional same-stage Climate & Energy companies.
